title: Ops Signal Fabric — Cross-Team Collaboration Agenda & Raw Notes (Apr 2026)
content:
Purpose: capture a lightweight, actionable plan for aligning telemetry (the 'signal fabric') across product, infra, and SRE to support pragmatic SLOs for model-serving endpoints. This is a working note — raw meeting minutes, hypotheses to test, and an ownership sketch.

Goals (what success looks like):
- Agreed minimal set of signals for 95th/99th latency, error rate, and throughput for top 10 model endpoints.
- One canonical SLO definition per service class (interactive, batch, streaming) with measurement window and burn-rate policy.
- End-to-end trace from api-gateway to KV cache to GPU host instrumented for the above signals.
- A short experiment (3 weeks) that validates alerts -> on-call runbook -> rollback policy.

Scope (what we will not do):
- Not changing model logic or inference code in this phase.
- Not adding long-retention analytics; short-term aggregations only.

Agenda for cross-team kickoff (Apr 6) — notes below:
1) Quick context (2m) — why unify signals now (Priya)
2) Data inventory: what exists today (Miguel)
3) SLO candidate definitions (Sasha)
4) Ownership & handoffs (Aaron)
5) Immediate experiments & tasks with owners (all)
6) Risks & blockers (open mic)

Raw meeting notes / decisions:
- Miguel: there are 3 existing latency metrics but each team tags them differently; we'll standardize tag: endpoint_name, model_variant, region.
- Decision: canonical latency metric name = inference.latency_ms (histogram) and exported to prometheus + OTLP.
- Sasha proposed SLOs: interactive endpoints -> 95th latency < 250ms over 30d window, error budget 0.5%. Team pushed for separate 1d fast window for alerting.
- Aaron called out capacity-induced tail latency; recommended adding a queue-depth signal to correlate spikes.

Experiment plan (3-week sprint):
Week 0 (prep, owner assignment): create dashboards, align tags, deploy histogram buckets. Owners: Miguel (telemetry), Leah (dashboards).
Week 1 (data collection): collect baseline for top 10 endpoints. Tagging fixes and minor exporter patches as needed. Owners: Miguel + infra eng.
Week 2 (alerting + runbook test): create alert that triggers when 95th latency > 250ms for 10m AND queue_depth > threshold. Run simulated traffic test; on-call practices runbook. Owners: Sasha + SRE oncall.
Week 3 (assessment & rollback policy writeup): evaluate burn rate, false positive rate, and recommend final SLO text for signoff. Owners: Priya + product lead.

Ownership matrix (sketch):
- Telemetry pipeline & metric naming: infra/telemetry (Miguel)
- Dashboarding & storyboards: observability (Leah)
- SLO definition & product impact: product-hosted-api (Sasha)
- Runbook & on-call play: site-reliability-engineering (Aaron)
- Experiment orchestration: program manager (Priya)

Acceptance criteria for experiment:
- All target endpoints emit inference.latency_ms with correct tags for >95% of requests during a 7-day baseline.
- Dashboard shows stable percentiles with <5% missing data.
- Alert triggers during synthetic spike and runbook run completes within 30 minutes.

Known risks & mitigations:
- Risk: exporter changes might add cardinality -> blow up telemetry cost. Mitigation: limit tag cardinality; sample variant ids; run cost estimate.
- Risk: noisy alerts from training jobs. Mitigation: add traffic-type label (prod vs internal) and exclude internal.
- Risk: owner bandwidth. Mitigation: defer noncritical instrumentation; scope to top 10 endpoints by qps.

Open questions (to resolve in follow-ups):
- Measurement window: 30d vs 90d for SLO compliance (product input required).
- How to treat degraded responses that are syntactically OK but semantically wrong (quality SLOs) — out of scope for this sprint.
- Which team owns synthetic traffic generation for on-call tests?

Immediate next steps (by Apr 9):
- Miguel: propose histogram buckets and tagging scheme (doc link in linked_artifacts).
- Leah: sketch dashboard wireframe and invite product to review.
- Sasha: draft SLO text for interactive endpoints and share with product owners.
- Aaron: draft a two-step runbook (alert -> validate -> traffic-shift) and schedule a tabletop test.
- Priya: coordinate weekly 30-minute check-ins Monday 9am PT for the 3-week experiment window.

Notes to self: keep this doc lean. We'll move a polished summary to Confluence after the experiment if acceptance criteria pass. Use JIRA epic INF-1427 for task tracking.

Appendix (quick glossary):
- Signal fabric: the minimal, consistent set of telemetry signals that allow cross-team decisions without deep digging per service.
- Burn rate: how fast an error budget is being consumed.
- Endpoint class: interactive (low latency), batch (throughput oriented), streaming (steady throughput).

End of notes.
